pageCache.text:
Interested in joining New Horizons Children's Academy in September 2027?
Join us for our Open Morning Tours to see our school in action and meet our staff and children. Spaces are limited so please secure your place by contacting our office on 0333 360 2115
Welcome to New Horizons Children’s Academy
Welcome to New Horizons Children’s Academy
Belong, Aspire, Achieve
We are a vibrant and inclusive three form entry Primary and Nursery School where there is a relentless ambition for all to succeed within a nurturing environment. We offer an aspirational learning experience as an Advanced Accredited Thinking Skills School enabling children to become articulate, critical, creative and reflective thinkers. We have high expectations for all children to excel achieving their best academically but also ensure they grow in personal qualities, self-confidence and motivation.
We have a highly dedicated staff team who work in close partnership with parents/carers to enable children to be their best self and help shape their success preparing them for their future.
We look forward to welcoming you to our happy, hardworking and ambitious school where we are committed to transforming the life chances of every individual.
Mrs Talbot-BrownHead of School
Quick Links
Curriculum Areas
School Times
term dates
Our Vision
Together we belong, aspire and achieve at New Horizons Children's academy, every child matters - we take time to know them well. Every moment of learning counts, and were committed to high standards ambitious teaching and a rich curriculum that empowers every pupil to be their best self.
Latest News & Updates
We are so proud of everyone who took part. Every donation, every dance, and every bit of encouragement has helped raise awareness and make a real difference.
What an incredible achievement! Thanks to the fantastic support of our pupils, families, and school community, Dance for Diabetes 2026 has now come to a close, and together we've raised an amazing amount to support children and young people living with diabetes.
Did you know that a child is classed as persistently absent if they miss 10% or more of school sessions across the academic year?

Welcome back to Term 6 — the final term of the academic year!

pageCache.pageTitle: Promoting British Values, New Horizons Children's Academy
pageCache.text:
Interested in joining New Horizons Children's Academy in September 2027?
Join us for our Open Morning Tours to see our school in action and meet our staff and children. Spaces are limited so please secure your place by contacting our office on 0333 360 2115
At New Horizons Children's Academy, we are committed to helping every child grow into a responsible, respectful, and active member of modern Britain. Through our curriculum, assemblies, and daily school life, we actively promote the fundamental British Values of Democracy, The Rule of Law, Individual Liberty, and Mutual Respect and Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
Our children are encouraged to share their ideas, understand right from wrong, celebrate diversity, and develop confidence in their own identities. By nurturing these principles from an early age, we aim to equip our children with the skills and attitudes they need to contribute positively to their community and the wider world.
“New Horizons Children’s Academy has a collaborative and family‑orientated approach where diversity, nurture, inspiration, and drive flourish in harmony.”
- Univerisity of Exeter, 2025
Fundamental British Values:

Interested in joining New Horizons Children's Academy in September 2027?
Join us for our Open Morning Tours to see our school in action and meet our staff and children. Spaces are limited so please secure your place by contacting our office on 0333 360 2115
High aspirations for all
At New Horizons, we want to transform the life chances of every child who walks through our door by providing an education which promotes aspiration, fosters a love of learning within a safe, purposeful and nurturing environment. We hold high aspirations and standards for all members of our school community and work in partnership with all stakeholders for the benefit of all of our children.
We want to make learning irresistible so that your child comes to school every day happy and eager to learn. We know that children are naturally inquisitive and we aim to develop this curiosity by providing a curriculum that engages and excites but also provides challenge at the correct level.
Admissions Policy 2025-2026
Admissions Policy 2026-2027
Admissions Policy 2027-2028
Nursery Admissions
Our Nursery takes children aged between 3 years and up to 5 years old.
Please note that attendance at our Nursery does not guarantee a place in our Reception classes.
Application Form
If you would like to apply for a place in the Nursery at New Horizons Children's Academy then please complete an application form and email to the school office. Alternatively, paper copies are available from the office.
Thank you for your interest and we will confirm spaces with you shortly.
Nursery Admissions Form
Nursery Admissions Policy
Nursery Admissions Poster
Reception Admissions
Apply by 15th January for a space in 2026 here: https://admissions.medway.gov.uk/Synergy/Admissions.aspx. You can now book in to our Prospective Family Parent Information Evening and book in a tour to see the school by clicking the button below.
Appeals
Appealing an offer for Year R
You can appeal for any school named on your application that has not been able to offer your child a place. To do this you will need to complete an appeal request form.
The form and details of where to return it to for each school will be published in the next steps guide on offer day.
The deadline for submitting an appeal is Thursday 14th May 2026 for offers made on 16th April 2026.
For late applications, appeals should be heard within 40 school days from the deadline for lodging appeals where possible, or within 30 school days of the appeal being lodged where reasonably possible in line with updated guidance from the Department for Education.
You can appeal after these deadlines but your appeal might not be heard at the same time as those submitted on-time.
When you appeal you:
Schools will not know you have appealed for another school unless you tell them. The appeals for each school are completely independent of each other.

All primary schools in England are provided with an amount of money which must be spent on Sport in school during the academic year.
Whilst the money itself is ‘ring fenced’, schools are free to determine how best to use this funding to improve the quality and breadth of PE and sport provision, including increasing participation in PE and sport so that all pupils develop healthy lifestyles and reach the performance levels they are capable of.

pageCache.pageTitle: Accredited Thinking School, New Horizons Children's Academy
pageCache.text:
Interested in joining New Horizons Children's Academy in September 2027?
Join us for our Open Morning Tours to see our school in action and meet our staff and children. Spaces are limited so please secure your place by contacting our office on 0333 360 2115
A Cognitive Approach to Education
As part of the Thinking Schools Academy Trust, we take pride in the unique approach we take to education: we provide our children with the skills and tools they need to think in a variety of ways and become lifelong learners. The transferrable Thinking Tools that we teach our pupils are designed to prepare them for the range of scenarios, dilemmas and circumstances that they may face in later life as part of modern society.
“To become a thinking school requires (shared) vision, skillful in-service training and a great deal of hard work. In one sense, the process is never-ending, but we do believe that schools demonstrating that they can match a certain number of basic criteria can rightfully claim to be a thinking school.” – Professor Bob Burden, of Exeter University.
We were delighted with University of Exeter's report, which highlighted the positive impact our thinking culture has had for our students:
What is a Thinking School?
A Thinking School is unique in their focus to share with your child the tools to become a life-long learner, and to develop the best possible habits for success in life. It is an educational community which involves both students and staff learning how to think reflectively, critically and creatively. A Thinking School is more than just a title, to become one the school has to earn the Thinking accreditation from Exeter University.
We want every student in our schools to be inquisitive and confident in themselves. Our thinking toolkit is how we support them through this journey. These tools are used in tandem with an approach to teaching that instils a growth mindest and ‘can do’ attitude. Through their time in a Thinking School, students will develop the right habits to ensure they are successful throughout education and beyond.
Thinking Tools and Strategies
Thinking Maps are eight graphic organisers that foster students’ abilities to see connections across their studies and encourage lifelong learning. Taken together they form a visual language of learning that is shared by staff and students.
Thinking Maps – A Guide
Thinking Hats provide a practical method of directed cognition. Each of six distinct types of thinking are represented by a different coloured hat. When an individual is ‘wearing’ a specific hat they focus their thinking in the associated manner. Consequently the method helps people be more productive, focused, and mindfully involved.
Thinking Hats - A Guide
Thinking Keys are a set of twenty different ways of approaching an issue or subject designed to engage and motivate learners in a range of thinking activities.
Thinking Keys– A Guide
